feedback.problem:
For the function

$$
G(s)=\frac{1}{s({s}^{2}+36)},\,s>0
$$

find the inverse Laplace transform of $G(s),$ given that
$L{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\omega t)}=\frac{\omega }{{s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2}}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that we can write $G(s)$ as 

$$
G(s)=\frac{1}{s({s}^{2}+36)}=\frac{F(s)}{s},
$$

where $F(s)=\frac{1}{{s}^{2}+36}.$
Also, we know that

$$
L{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\omega t)}=\frac{\omega }{{s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2}}.
$$

Thus, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}{F(s)} & ={L}^{-1}\,{\frac{1}{{s}^{2}+36}} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\,{\frac{1}{6}\cdot \frac{6}{{s}^{2}+36}} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\,{L}^{-1}\,{\frac{6}{{s}^{2}+{6}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\,sin\,(6t).\end{aligned}
$$

Additionally, we know that if $L{f(t)}=F(s)$, then

$$
L{{\int }_{0}^{t}f(τ)\,\text{d}τ}=\frac{F(s)}{s}.
$$

Using the property above in reverse, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}{G(s)} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{F(s)}{s}} \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}f(τ)\,\text{d}τ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}\frac{1}{6}\,sin\,(6τ)\,\text{d}τ \\  & =-\frac{1}{36}cos\,(6τ)\,{|}_{0}^{t} \\  & =\frac{1}{36}(1-cos\,(6t)).\end{aligned}
$$
